lede.p1: Legal Practicum is an innovative teaching and learning tool for law students and lawyers. Legal Practicum is designed for lawyers at any level.  It is a living teaching and learning method that can be revised and improved as technology changes.
lede.p2: Try an experiment. Take a risk. Receive immediate feedback. Try again. Any time. No waiting in line. No coffee breaks. 24/7. A classroom of one. It is yours whenever you want.

after_skills.p1:
For more than 50 years, a group of exceptional people — law students, law professors, lawyers from firms large and small, judges, and non-lawyers — have worked together to develop Legal Practicum to help law students and lawyers learn not simply the law, but how to practice it.

Legal Practicum provides an environment in which participants can develop and refine their skills, experiment with different approaches, test ideas, strategies, and techniques, effectively use and manage technology, and take risks without fear of negative consequences. It is an opportunity to learn through experience, make mistakes, and grow as a legal practitioner.
after_skills.p2: Emerging technologies will help lawyers at all levels of experience provide legal services more quickly and at a reasonable cost. The goal: justice for all.
after_skills.p3: Legal Practicum is an open resource available at no cost to law students and lawyers at all stages of their careers. It may be modified and adapted to any jurisdiction and used to develop, enhance, and refine legal practice and law practice management skills.

sonsteng.name: John Sonsteng
sonsteng.bio: John Sonsteng is an emeritus professor at Mitchell Hamline School of Law. He was a trial lawyer before he became a teacher. John has written many books and articles about advocacy. He is a Fulbright scholar and has taught effective advocacy skills throughout the United States and in many other countries.

riehl.name: Damien Riehl
riehl.bio: Damien Riehl is a lawyer-technologist with deep experience in litigation, cybersecurity, and AI. Admitted in 2002 and coding since 1985, he clerked for chief judges, litigated complex cases, and led global digital forensics teams. He now builds AI-driven legal systems. He co-chairs Minnesota's Connected and Automated Vehicles Council and chairs the MSBA AI Committee, advancing access-to-justice initiatives. He helped develop SALI's 18,000+ legal data standards and contributes to FOLIO's legal ontology. At Clio, he integrates AI into large-scale legal datasets. He also engages AI ethics work with global Catholic leaders and created the "All the Music" public-domain project.

breit.name: Abby Breit
breit.bio:
Abby Breit is an attorney, business owner, and President of More Than Money Trust Company. Her work focuses on trust administration, family stewardship, and technology development.

While attending Mitchell Hamline School of Law, Abby worked closely with John Sonsteng as Student Director of the Center for Law and Business. John became a trusted mentor and close friend and continues to be an important source of guidance in her life.

Her work in family stewardship reflects her appreciation for asking difficult questions, listening, and understanding others. Abby is grateful for the opportunity to support John and Damien in helping students and lawyers learn not only the law, but how to practice it.

sample.title: Watch a sample consultation ▸
sample.description: A recorded client interview — Devon Halvard, charged with DWI — played back turn by turn, then assessed with feedback. See the consultation room and the debrief in action before you bring your own key. Scripted sample, not a live AI client.

matters.description: Ten practice shapes, each in the fictional State of Meridian and again in a real jurisdiction. Full packets, case files, rubrics, and interviews.

firm.title: Firm dashboard
firm.description: Ellingboe & Ravndal LLP — the two-lawyer practicum firm. Fees, realization, AR aging, trust accounting, and budget, charted and taught.

templates.title: Deliverable templates
templates.description: The six recurring course handouts — time sheet, engagement letter, interview plan, settlement plan, portfolio, and reflective report — each presented as a Planning Guide and Checklist with assessment and feedback notes. Print-ready.

centaur.title: People first; technology as the tool
centaur.description: Every exercise here ships with a machine-readable rubric and a revise-and-repeat loop. Faculty coach students through live work with people. Technology supplies more practice repetitions under faculty supervision. Technology gives the first-pass assessment and feedback, at any hour. The simulated client interviews, rubric feedback, and firm dashboard below support that practice.

getting_started.title: Getting started at your school
getting_started.description: Meet the people who run the practicum, shape it around your school, and find free matters and templates to begin.
